data.why: Integrating multiple acquired companies is a massive headache for a Corporate Controller, directly impacting the month-end close. It is specific, recent, and ties perfectly to the Block case study.
data.angle: Folding new companies into the close creates manual work reconciling different sets of books.

not_chosen.reason: Bad news: Awkward to mention a job post for his own role (Corporate Controller), which might imply he is being replaced.
Bad news: Mentions supply chains struggling to keep up, which is a negative industry trend.
Sources disagree on the funding amount ($630M in s7 vs $730M in s11), and every other rep will pitch the funding round.
Strong hook, but AP/invoice processing is slightly less relevant to a Corporate Controller than the month-end close impact of acquisitions.
Good signal of accounting workload, but the recent acquisitions are a more specific trigger for close complexity.

data.subject: recent acquisitions
data.body:
Hi Sanjiv,

Saw CesiumAstro acquired 1Aardvark and Jariet Technologies recently. Integrating new businesses into your accounting processes usually means your team is stuck manually reconciling different sets of books to get the month-end close done.

Block removed 75% of human touchpoints in the accounting close with Zamp.

Open to seeing how?

[Your name]
